system.summary: the royal cipher “A” of Philip IV’s letters to Santa Cruz (1629–1632), also used by the Infanta in Brussels: a homophonic syllabary (letter groups pan = ca, fan = que, sol = por…, numbers 1–99 for syllables and letters) and a nomenclator (numbers 100–260 and groups for names: 128 Emperador, 194 guerra, 222 Italia, tus paz, hon Piamonte…).

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 725 open; nothing in this repository on the Santa Cruz fonds; no edition found (web search 28 Oct 2026). A plain-text draft at Simancas (AGS Estado, Milán, 1630) is possible but undescribed and not consulted.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Inventory of 9 PARES units of no. 725-727 (Santa Cruz C.50-51): three keys (A 1629-1632, B 1632, C 1635); about 30 contemporary decipherments.
Key A learnt by EM alignment on contemporary cipher/decipherment pairs; successive keys K1-K5 frozen and checked on held-out pairs (D.53 0.70, D.188 0.73, D.163 0.84, D.175 0.87 words).
K6A: K5 pairs + D.163, D.175 + the Infanta's D.31/D.32 (same key, found by another agent).
K6A on D.167/D.168, never opened before (pre-registered): 0.752 words, 0.857 characters vs 200 permuted controls p99 0.257 / 0.591.
D.213 transcribed in full (7 pages) and read; probable and restored words justified one by one.

texts.label: Philip IV to the Marquis of Santa Cruz, Madrid, 6 December 1630 (AHNOB SANTA CRUZ,C.50,D.213)
texts.summary: October 1630: before besieged Casale, the French and Spanish armies are about to fight when a young papal envoy, Giulio Mazarini, rides between the lines and wrests an agreement. On 6 December Philip IV answers his governor of Milan, the Marquis of Santa Cruz, in cipher: he approves the agreement, which “restored the reputation” of a discredited Emperor, wants a peace concluded before March, orders a secret inquiry into the army’s unreadiness, insists that Casale and Mantua stay guarded by the Emperor and that the Milanese be fortified — “and above all do not spend a single real badly”.

reading_review.note: reading.md and translation.md read as sentences: five long chancery paragraphs (Vilani's arrival and the Casale agreement of Mazarini; seek a better peace but conclude by March; the answer to the Duke of Savoy and the inquiry into the army; fortify the Milanese and spend nothing badly). The nine unresolved words (29, 28, lor, nat, dol x2, dul, mur, fri) leave every sentence parseable; 28 probable and 22 restored words are marked and justified in NOTES.
